description: 🚀 Voyager is a multidisciplinary team of developers, AI enthusiasts, and designers united by a passion for space exploration. We combine technology, creativity, and NASA data to build innovative solutions for real-world challenges.
summary:
ASTRO COMMANDER
NASA Space Apps Cairo 2026 | Challenge: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer | Team: VOYAGER-X

Astro Commander is a pixel-art browser game where teens (12-17) command an outpost on the Moon or Mars for a 10-day mission. They must keep energy, oxygen, water and radiation protection above zero, and every action has a cost. It works offline, installs as an app, and supports Arabic and English.

Players choose an astronaut and rocket, land, explore in real gravity, collect samples, drive a rover, and complete science labs and a special mission.

Storm Shelter: a base built beside the lander. When a storm warning appears, players can run inside to stay safe, but it costs energy and oxygen and gives fewer points than facing the storm.

Tutorial: 17 interactive steps that react to the player's actions, with science explanations, a storm drill, quizzes and clear, highly visible panels.

NASA data: the game uses the DONKI API (solar flares, CMEs and solar particle events from the last 30 days). Real events shape each mission day and storm. It clearly shows live or stored data and uses real saved records offline.

Built with Phaser 3, JavaScript, HTML and CSS.

dataRefs: NASA's central public API portal, providing free programmatic access to datasets including the Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD), Mars Rover Photos, and the Space Weather Database (DONKI). A free API key (higher rate limits than the shared demo key) can be requested instantly and is a good starting point for any challenge team building a data-connected prototype.
